items.q: Child after nasal trauma with boggy bilateral septal swelling needs what urgently?
items.exp: Septal haematoma strips cartilage nutrition causing necrosis, saddle deformity and abscess; prompt incision drainage plus packing and antibiotics prevents cartilage loss. Delay deforms growing noses.
r: Incorrect. Week delay necroses cartilage.
Correct. Drain septal haematoma urgently.
Incorrect. Packing without drainage traps blood.
Incorrect. Boggy septum after trauma is haematoma until drained.
items.kp: Boggy septum after blow: drain today.

items.q: Neonate cyanosed when quiet, pink when crying, NG tube will not pass nose suggests what?
items.exp: Obligate nasal breathing infants suffocate with bilateral choanal block and relieve by mouth breathing when crying; failed tube passage confirms nasal obstruction needing airway and endoscopic opening.
r: Incorrect. Laryngomalacia stridors without tube failure pattern.
Correct. Bilateral choanal atresia classic picture.
Incorrect. Fistula chokes with feeds and distends abdomen.
Incorrect. Aspiration distresses continuously from birth.
items.kp: Blue quiet, pink crying newborn: blocked choanae.

items.q: CHARGE association includes choanal atresia plus which features?
o: Cardiac defects, coloboma and ear anomalies
items.exp: CHARGE: Coloboma, Heart defects, Atresia choanae, Retarded growth, Genital and Ear anomalies, so atresia babies need cardiology, eye and hearing assessment. Others are isolated distractors.
r: Correct. Heart, eye and ear anomalies accompany atresia.
Incorrect. Goitre belongs to Pendred hearing syndrome.
Incorrect. Polydactyly alone does not define CHARGE.
Incorrect. Renal cysts point elsewhere (for example VACTERL renal).
items.kp: Atretic choanae: check heart, eyes and ears.

items.q: Septal perforation with saddle nose, epistaxis and systemic illness suggests which systemic cause?
items.exp: Vasculitic septal destruction with saddle, crusting and pulmonary renal disease marks granulomatosis with polyangiitis (ANCA associated), needing systemic workup before local repair. Cocaine is the other classic cause.
r: Incorrect. Allergy sneezes without destroying septum.
Correct. Vasculitis destroys septum and saddles nose.
Incorrect. Deviation bows but does not perforate systemically.
Incorrect. Sinusitis is acute infection without saddle.
items.kp: Perforated saddle nose plus systemic signs: vasculitis.

items.q: Closed reduction of nasal fracture is best timed when?
o: After swelling settles, within about 2 weeks
items.exp: Reducing after oedema falls (days) but before bone sets (about 2 weeks adults, sooner children) restores alignment accurately. Septal haematoma alone cannot wait for this window.
r: Incorrect. Swelling hides true alignment.
Correct. After swelling, before union sets.
Incorrect. Months later needs osteotomy surgery.
Incorrect. Displaced fractures benefit from timely reduction.
items.kp: Wait days for swelling, not weeks for setting.

items.q: Whistling on breathing with crusting and nosebleeds suggests which septal lesion?
items.exp: Air through a septal hole whistles while turbulent drying crusts and bleeds; causes include surgery, cocaine and vasculitis. Examination and cause control precede obturator or closure decisions.
r: Incorrect. Haematoma is acute boggy swelling.
Correct. Perforation whistles and crusts.
Incorrect. Spurs obstruct without whistling hole.
Incorrect. Choanal polyps block posteriorly without whistle.
items.kp: Nose that whistles has a hole in it.

items.q: Unilateral choanal atresia typically presents how in childhood?
o: Persistent one sided nasal discharge and blockage
items.exp: One open side sustains breathing, so unilateral atresia declares later as single sided mucoid discharge and obstruction, sometimes found at adenoid or sinus assessment. Bilateral disease is neonatal emergency.
r: Incorrect. Cyanosis marks bilateral neonatal block.
Correct. One sided discharge in child.
Incorrect. Smell loss is bilateral mucosal disease clue.
Incorrect. Bleeding alone points to vessels or masses.
items.kp: One blocked nostril since childhood: unilateral atresia.

items.q: Septoplasty preserves which structure to prevent saddle deformity?
o: Dorsal and caudal L strut of cartilage
items.exp: Retaining an L shaped dorsal caudal cartilage strut maintains nasal support while deviated central cartilage is corrected; over resection (old SMR) risked saddle and tip collapse.
r: Incorrect. Vomer work does not support dorsum.
Correct. Preserve the L strut.
Incorrect. Alar cartilages shape tip, not septal support strut.
Incorrect. Bones support upper third only.
items.kp: Keep the L, keep the nose shape.

items.q: Most nasal septal deviations cause which management need?
o: None when asymptomatic; treat only obstruction or access problems
items.exp: Minor deviations are normal anatomy; surgery follows symptomatic obstruction failing medical therapy, contact symptoms or surgical access needs, not radiographic deviation alone.
r: Incorrect. Imaging deviation alone never mandates surgery.
Correct. Treat symptoms, not scans.
Incorrect. Steroids treat mucosal rhinitis, not bone shape.
Incorrect. Packing treats bleeding acutely.
items.kp: Operate on blocked patients, not bent pictures.

items.q: Anterior septal bleeding site Kiesselbach plexus lies in which named area?
items.exp: Little area on anterior inferior septum hosts Kiesselbach plexus anastomosis, source of most epistaxis and target of pressure and cautery. Posterior bleeds arise deeper from sphenopalatine branches.
r: Correct. Little area anterior septum.
Incorrect. Choana is posterior outlet.
Incorrect. Meatus drains sinuses laterally.
Incorrect. Olfactory cleft is superior smell region.
items.kp: Front septum plexus is Little area.
